Question: How do you see seat sharing agreement between RJD and Congress in Bihar for 2024 Lok Sabha election?
Answer: It is becoming quite evident that Lalu Yadav is remotely controlling the Bihar Congress unit with the help of Bihar Congress President Akhilesh Prasad Singh. Akhilesh Prasad Singh is an old associate of Lalu Prasad Yadav and was a Central Minister (MoS) in the First Manmohan Singh Cabinet from the RJD quota. Akhilesh Prasad Singh left RJD and joined Congress in 2010 but his equation with the Lalu family has remained intact. A few months ago, Akhilesh Prasad Singh conducted a secret deal with Lalu Yadav in which Akhilesh Prasad Singh got the Rajya Sabha seat with RJD’s help and gave up the MLC seat. Congress high command in Delhi was kept in the dark over the deal and the high command had assumed that Congress would get at least one MLC seat. The division of seats in INDIA Alliance in Bihar is - 26 seats for RJD, 9 for Congress, 3 for CPI(ML), 1 for CPI, and 1 for CPI(M). The two most popular leaders of Bihar Congress are Pappu Yadav and Kanhaiya Kumar. Akhilesh Prasad Singh has made sure that these two leaders don’t get their seats as he fears that these two leaders can overshadow him. Priyanka Gandhi had promised Pappu Yadav that he would get Purnea seat but Lalu Yadav lobbied with Akhilesh Prasad Singh to deny Pappu Yadav this seat. Congress easily gave up its claim on the Begusarai seat. Another big Congress leader in Bihar is former Delhi DGP & former Governor Nikhil Kumar (who is also the son of a former CM). His family has won the seat 8 times but this time he has been denied the chance to fight the election. Interestingly, Congress gave up Valmiki Nagar seat to take up Paschim Champaran. Last time Congress had narrowly lost Valmiki Nagar by just 22K votes and this time they would have given a very tough fight to NDA in this seat. There are rumors that Akhilesh Prasad Singh is lobbying for his son and that’s why he gave up the Valmiki Nagar seat. Congress has a realistic chance on two Muslim-dominated seats - Katihar and Kishganganj and Congress will field Muslim candidates from these two seats. Some of the very weak seats like Patna Sahib and Samastipur (SC) have been given by the alliance to Congress. This seat sharing shows that Lalu Yadav is more worried about the 2025 Assembly election and he wants to make his son Tejashwi Yadav the number one Yadav leader in Bihar. Pappu Yadav could have won Purnea seat but Lalu Yadav is ready to lose some seats to weaken Pappu Yadav. He also has denied Kanhaiya Kumar the Begusarai seat. This time, he has been doing some experiments like giving more tickets to the Kushwaha community to attract more Kushwaha votes (which is a solid vote bank of NDA). Lalu Yadav has distributed his party symbol to many RJD candidates even before the finalization of seat-sharing agreement. This is a signal to Congress that he is the boss of Bihar and Congress has no option other than becoming “C” team of RJD. NDA has announced candidates on 37 seats and INDIA alliance has not announced even a single candidate. Even though many RJD candidates have privately received symbol from RJD. As of now, it’s an advantage for NDA in Bihar because of the arrogance of Lalu Yadav.

Question: What are the key differences between a democratic and an authoritarian form of government?
Answer: I would answer this question with one dimension - freedom to criticize Government or display dissident. The best examples of authoritarian Government is China and Russia and the example of democratic Government is India, US, Europe etc. What happens if you don’t agree with idea of the Supreme Leader/PM/President or critisze them - The another key difference between democracy and autocracy is that Democratic leaders face “real elections” in every 4 to 5 years. There are some kind of restrictive or rigged election in autocracy but general public is not allowed to freely vote in those countries.

Question: Do you think Nitish Kumar can join the NDA again in 2024?
Answer: Nitish Kumar is an ultimate “Paltu Ram” in Indian politics. He is never committed in any alliance & always keeps back channel open with the other party. He is a master politician who knows how to survive in politics & enjoy power. He has been in power (in Centre and Bihar) since 1998 (except one and half year in 2004–05). He is never afraid of dumping his partners and joining a new alliance (or forming his party). One day he can be your friend and tomorrow he can be your enemy. He is a very shrewd politician with one weakness - desire to become PM or at least a national leader. His wish to become a national leader has permanently damager his political reputation and Bihar. Image Source - Hindustan Times Nitish dumped BJP & left NDA in August 2022 & joined the Grand alliance with RJD, Congress and Left parties. The opposition parties (Congress, RJD etc.) promised him that he can become PM candidate or at least convener of the anti-Modi alliance (which later became INDI alliance). After that, Nitish toured the whole India and met with many opposition leaders. He was pivotal in bringing many non-Congress opposition parties in opposition alliance. But Congress started to ignore him after Karnataka election win and assumed the central role in the INDI alliance. Even after many meetings, Nitish has not been named convener of INDI alliance and Mamata Banerjee along with Kejriwal rocked Nitish Kumar’s boat by proposing the name of Mallikarjun Kharge as PM candidate. In fact, Congress & other parties have been very slow in seat sharing and creating a common minimum program for the INDI alliance. Nitish Kumar has publicly expressed his anger at the slow progress of INDI alliance. On the other hand, Lalu Yadav wants to make his 9th fail son Tejashwi Yadav CM soon. There might have been a deal between Nitish & Lalu that Nitish would become opposition alliance convener / PM candidate and he would vacate Bihar CM’s post for Tejashwi Yadav. Now, RJD is putting immense pressure on Nitish Kumar to resign as CM of Bihar but Nitish is not ready to do the same. RJD and its alliance partners (except JD(U)) have 115 MLAs in Bihar and they just need 7 more MLAs to form Government in Bihar. As Nitish was and still is not ready to make Tejashwi CM, there are allegations thar Lalu Yadav has been conspiring with former JD(U) national president Lalan Singh to sideline Nitish Kumar. There are rumors that Lalan Singh had 12 MLAs in his camp and he might have expelled these MLAs on some pretext (by being the national President) so that these MLAs would not have lost their membership. Tejashwi Yadav would have become CM with help of these 12 MLAs and Lalan Singh would have either become deputy CM or a Rajya Sabha member. It seems that Nitish Kumar got wind of the plan and now he has removed Lalan Singh and JD(U) national president. It also seems that now those 12 MLAs have fallen in line and they are with Nitish Kumar now. It seems that most of JD(U) sitting MPs and inner circle of Nitish Kumar want to go with BJP. Meanwhile, BJP also doen’t want to see Tejashwi Yadav as Bihar CM. As of today BJP’s Mohan Yadav is the only Yadav CM in India and BJP wants to make inroads into Yadav vote bank in North India (for at least Lok Sabha elections). The RJD-Congress-Left and JD(U) alliance is very strong on paper in Bihar. BJP has 17 MPs from Bihar and they may be able to retain these seats but crossing 20 seats would be a daunting task for BJP in Bihar. ALl the pre-poll surveys are showing almost equal split of Lok Sabha seats in Bihar between NDA and INDI Allaince. Last time, NDA (BJP-JD(U) and LJP) won 39 seats in Bihar and even this time the alliance may win 35 plus seats easily. So, despite the reluctance of BJP supporters and leaders, BJP national leadership might go with Nitish Kumar if the opportunity comes. Its a well known fact that Nitish Kumar feels more ease in NDA than in alliance with Lalu Yadav. But his desire to become a national leader has forced him to ally with Lalu Yadav twice in the last decade. Nitish Kumar is becoming politically weaker day by day and now there are question marks over the future of his party. He is becoming highly unpopular and both BJP and RJD want to sideline him but they can’t do this yet. As his national ambition has evaporated, he may want to re-join NDA (obviously with less bargaining power). Ideally BJP would like CM post for itself but Nitish Kumar may not accept this condition. He may accept less Lok Sabha seats than 2019. Nitish may also want simultaneous Lok Sabha and assembly poll but BJP may not accept this. RJD may be a bigger loser in this game. Irrespective of Nitish’s future move, Tejashwi Yadav may not become CM before 2025 assembly election and at worst they may end up in opposition. We don’t know what would happen in Bihar in 2024. There are two possibilities - 1) Nitish may go back to NDA or 2) Nitish may be using the opportunity & negotiations with BJP to keep Lalu Yadav in check while being in INDI Alliance.
